question.text: The NIFTY Alpha Low-Volatility 30 index selects 30 stocks based on a rule combining 50% weight on Alpha and 50% weight on Low Volatility factors. This is an example of:

explanation.text: The Logic: Smart beta uses pre-defined, rule-based factor tilts (here alpha + low-vol) to construct the index — systematic but not a simple market-cap-weighted broad index. The Trap: It isn't 'pure passive' because factor rules introduce manager judgement at index-design stage. It isn't 'active' either — rebalancing is mechanical once rules are set. Cross-Exam Context: Appears in X-A Investment Adviser as a product category; XXI-B treats it as a construction technique. Manager's Pro-Tip: Factors that work historically can underperform for long stretches — smart-beta drawdowns can test investor patience even though fees are low.
